title: Wine tannins: Where are they coming from? A method to access the importance of berry part on wine tannins content
author: Rousserie, Lacampagne, et al.

steps.title: Determine sampling time points
steps.instruction: Identify four sampling moments for each modality (berry, seed, skin wine): (i) half alcoholic fermentation when density reaches 1.030, (ii) end of alcoholic fermentation when density reaches 0.990, (iii) middle of post‑fermentative maceration ≈ one week after the end of alcoholic fermentation, and (iv) end of post‑fermentative maceration ≈ two weeks after the end of alcoholic fermentation.

steps.title: Collect wine sample
steps.instruction: At each identified sampling moment, withdraw 20 mL of wine from the fermenter.

steps.title: Remove corresponding vegetal material
steps.instruction: Immediately after withdrawing the wine, remove from the fermenter the amount of vegetal material that corresponds to the sampled juice to keep the vegetal‑material‑to‑juice ratio constant: for the berry modality remove berries, for the seed modality remove seeds, and for the skin modality remove skins.

steps.title: Calculate vegetal material mass
steps.instruction: Compute the mass of vegetal material taken using the formula given in the article: Vegetalmaterialweight = Totalamountofvegetalmaterialinfermenter900×20.
